name: Voice
summary: Hears you with Whisper and answers out loud — in Piper on this machine, in Qwen3-TTS if you have the Python for it, or in a voice cloned from a clip of your own.

requires.why: To hear you when you speak. The recording is turned into text here and the sound is not kept.
To read an answer out loud through your speakers.
To open a recording you point it at.
To keep Whisper and the speech model in a folder of its own.
To fetch Whisper and Piper once from GitHub, and a speech model and a voice once from Hugging Face.
To run Whisper, Piper and Qwen here rather than sending anything away to be listened to or read out.
To browse the voices published on fish.audio and to speak in one, and only once you have added a key.

settings.label: Voice engine
settings.hint: Which of them speaks. Everything below is the material that one works with — what does not apply to it is not on this page.

options.label: Piper
options.hint: Fast, and entirely on this machine. Three published voices and any .onnx you bring. It cannot clone a voice and has no expression at all.

options.label: Qwen3-TTS
options.hint: Better than Piper, still on this machine, and the only local engine that can clone a voice from a recording. It wants a Python with qwen-tts in it and a graphics card.
options.reason: Point “Qwen program” at a Python that has qwen-tts installed — it is at the bottom of this page.

options.label: fish.audio
options.hint: A cloud engine: fast, no graphics card, and it can clone from fifteen seconds. What you say is read exactly as written, and it leaves this machine to be spoken.
options.reason: Add a fish.audio key at the bottom of this page.

options.label: fish.audio, with expression
options.hint: The same, with each reply marked up for emotion first. One extra model call per reply, and it is the only engine here that can be told how to say something.
options.reason: Add a fish.audio key at the bottom of this page.

widgets.label: Find a voice
widgets.hint: A name to look for among the voices published on fish.audio. Leave it empty to see what the filters alone turn up.

widgets.label: Language
widgets.hint: Language codes. Most of the catalogue is not English, so leaving all of them off answers in languages you cannot judge.

widgets.label: Kind of voice
widgets.hint: The vendor's own words for its voices. Several together narrow it.

widgets.label: Search fish.audio
widgets.hint: Asks again with whatever is in the boxes above, and fills the list below.

widgets.label: Voices on fish.audio
widgets.hint: The top few for what you searched, in their authors' own words. Play the sample, or hear one say your own line, then keep it — a kept voice joins the list below and can speak without ever being downloaded.

widgets.label: Preview text
widgets.default: This is what I sound like.
widgets.placeholder: This is what I sound like.
widgets.hint: What a voice says when you ask to hear it. One line for the whole page, because the question is what the voices sound like rather than what each one says.

widgets.label: Your voices
widgets.hint: Every voice this machine can reach, under the engine it belongs to. The one that speaks is the chosen voice of the engine picked at the top; choosing a voice under another engine sets that engine's voice, and pick the engine to hear it.

widgets.label: Add a Piper voice
widgets.hint: A .onnx voice you have downloaded, with its .onnx.json beside it. Choose the .onnx here, then press Add.

widgets.label: …and its .onnx.json
widgets.hint: The settings file that came with it. Piper will not load a voice without one — it is where the sample rate lives, so half a voice is silence rather than an error.

widgets.label: Add the voice above
widgets.hint: Copies the file into Alexia. Piper cannot clone a voice from a recording — this is for one you have already downloaded.

widgets.label: A recording to clone
widgets.hint: Fifteen seconds of the voice you want. Put the words that were said in the box below, then press Clone.

widgets.label: What the recording says
widgets.placeholder: The exact words spoken in the clip.
widgets.hint: A cloner told what was said makes a better voice than one guessing.

widgets.label: Clone the voice in the recording
widgets.hint: Uses the recording and the words above. On fish.audio the clip and its transcript leave this machine and the voice lives on that account until you remove it here; on Qwen3-TTS neither leaves.

widgets.label: Hearing — speech model
widgets.hint: What Whisper turns your speech into text with, whichever engine answers. Bigger is more accurate and slower: tiny is 75 MB, base 148 MB, small 488 MB.

widgets.label: Processor threads
widgets.hint: More is faster until it is not. Four suits most machines.

widgets.label: Download now
widgets.hint: Fetches Whisper, Piper, the speech model and the voice. It happens on first use anyway; this is for getting it over with while you are looking.

widgets.label: Whisper program
widgets.hint: Leave this empty and Alexia downloads one. Point it at your own whisper-cli if you have a build that suits this machine better.

widgets.label: Piper program
widgets.hint: The same again for speaking. Empty means Alexia fetches one; on a machine with no prebuilt Piper this is how you supply your own.

widgets.label: Qwen program
widgets.hint: A Python that already has qwen-tts installed. Nothing here downloads PyTorch: a plugin that quietly pulls six gigabytes because somebody asked for a voice has decided something for you.

widgets.label: fish.audio key
widgets.hint: Needed for either fish.audio engine. Leave it empty and everything stays on this machine.
